clue.text: Why be ratty strangely about son's university?

indicators.note: about means going round, so the rearranged letters wrap around another piece
words behaving strangely are out of their normal order, so the letters get rearranged

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged
S is the standard abbreviation for son

explanation.surface: Someone asks why a student is so bad-tempered about the university their son attends.
explanation.walkthrough: The rearranged letters make ABERYTWYTH, and S slips in to give ABERYSTWYTH.
explanation.definitionFit: Aberystwyth is a Welsh seaside town whose university is part of the University of Wales, so the place name stands for the institution.

clue.text: Tactless spy unmasked

definitions.meaning: first meaning: speaking bluntly, without diplomacy
second meaning: Anthony ..., art historian exposed as a Soviet spy in 1979

explanation.walkthrough: Anthony Blunt, keeper of the Queen's pictures, was publicly exposed in 1979 as the 'fourth man' of the Cambridge spy ring.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective means frank to the point of rudeness, and the surname belongs to a famous exposed Soviet agent.

clue.text: US city detectives right over arresting a reformer

indicators.note: in a down clue, over means turned upside down, so the preceding letters read from the bottom up
to arrest someone is to hold them, so the letters surround the next piece

parts.note: LA is Los Angeles
CID is the Criminal Investigation Department of British police
R is the abbreviation for right
taken as written

explanation.surface: Police in an American city have arrested a political reformer.
explanation.walkthrough: LA, CID and R read backwards give RDICAL, which holds A to make RADICAL.
explanation.definitionFit: A radical is someone who wants sweeping political or social change, so a reformer in the stronger sense.

clue.text: Disheartened missing sport

indicators.note: losing heart means losing the middle, so the centre letters of the word are removed

parts.note: skipping a class means missing it

explanation.surface: Someone is downcast at missing out on their favourite sport.
explanation.walkthrough: SKIPPING loses its middle PP to leave SKIING.
explanation.definitionFit: Skiing, travelling over snow on long runners, is a winter sport.

clue.text: Glaring angrily, playwright you once ultimately married

parts.note: Oscar Wilde, the Irish playwright
ye is the old form of you

indicators.note: ultimately points to the end, so only the final letter of the next word is used

parts.note: the final letter of married

explanation.surface: Someone stares furiously, perhaps at a playwright who finally married.
explanation.definitionFit: Wild-eyed describes someone staring with fierce or frantic emotion, a close match for glaring angrily.

clue.text: Leaves old explorer heading north outside Chad's capital

indicators.note: in a down clue, heading north means travelling upwards, so the letters read from bottom to top

parts.note: O is the abbreviation for old

indicators.note: outside means surrounding, so the turned letters go round the next piece

parts.note: John Cabot, the Venetian explorer of North America

indicators.note: the capital of a word is its first letter

parts.note: the first letter of Chad

explanation.surface: An old explorer travels north around the capital of Chad.
explanation.walkthrough: O and CABOT read upwards give TOBACO, which wraps round C. 'Leaves' looks like a verb, but it is the noun.
explanation.definitionFit: Tobacco is the dried and cured leaves of the tobacco plant, smoked or chewed.

clue.text: Inadequate and roundabout ways to find electrical faults

parts.note: short means not enough
circuits are routes that go round

explanation.surface: Indirect and insufficient methods are used to track down wiring problems.
explanation.definitionFit: A short circuit is an electrical fault where current takes an unintended low-resistance path.

clue.text: Trick using heart he refused providing diamonds

indicators.note: what is refused is turned away, so those letters are dropped from the word

parts.note: heart with the letters of he taken off
providing means on condition that, i.e. if
ice is slang for diamonds

explanation.surface: A card player pulls a trick, refusing to play hearts and leading diamonds instead.
explanation.walkthrough: HEART minus HE leaves ART. Ice is criminal slang for diamonds.
explanation.definitionFit: Artifice is cunning or deception, a clever trick to mislead.

clue.text: When working, what butchers observe in human nature

definitions.meaning: first meaning, playful: the meat and gore a butcher sees on the job
second meaning: the physical, mortal side of people

explanation.walkthrough: The first half is a cryptic hint taking the phrase literally as meat and blood on the butcher's block.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means ordinary human nature with all its weaknesses, as in 'only flesh and blood'.

clue.text: Pester husband to approach bank miles away

indicators.note: with the miles gone away, the abbreviation for miles is removed

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for husband
a bank of earth is a mound

explanation.surface: A wife urges her husband to go up to a riverbank far away.
explanation.walkthrough: MOUND loses its M (miles) and follows H.
explanation.definitionFit: To hound someone is to pursue or harass them relentlessly, as a hunting dog chases prey.

clue.text: Some declare bill is regressive and prejudiced

indicators.note: regressive means going backwards, so the letters read right to left
some means only part of the following words is used

parts.note: letters running across the three words

explanation.surface: A politician calls a new law backward-looking and biased.
explanation.definitionFit: Illiberal means intolerant or narrow-minded, opposed to liberal ideas, which fits prejudiced.

clue.text: Recent moves involving retiring City international reserve

indicators.note: retiring means withdrawing or going back, so the following letters are read backwards
to involve is to take in, so the shuffled letters enclose the other piece
when the letters move about they end up in a new order

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged
EC is the postcode for the City of London
I is the abbreviation for international

explanation.surface: Recent transfers involve a City player retiring from the international reserve team.
explanation.walkthrough: The City of London is identified by its postcode letters; 'reserve' here is the noun for restraint, not a substitute player.
explanation.definitionFit: Reserve as a noun means restraint in speech or manner, which is what reticence is.

clue.text: Food items one has in casino?

definitions.meaning: second meaning: the tokens a gambler bets with

explanation.walkthrough: Chips in Britain are what Americans call fries.
explanation.definitionFit: Chips are fried potato strips, and also the plastic counters used for betting at a gaming table.

clue.text: Unfriendly nation, it's said

indicators.note: it's said means the word is spoken, so the answer matches its sound rather than spelling

parts.note: the South American country

explanation.surface: A country has a reputation for being unwelcoming.
explanation.definitionFit: A chilly reception is a cold, unwelcoming one, so the word works figuratively for frosty manners.

clue.text: This writer's phone gets fixed

parts.note: this writer is the setter, I, and I's means I am
a mobile is a cell phone

explanation.surface: The setter's telephone gets repaired.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fixed' looks like repaired, but it means stuck in place. 'This writer' is the crossword convention for the setter.
explanation.definitionFit: Immobile means unable to move, fixed in position.

clue.text: Type of pudding, one Liam's cooked

indicators.note: cooked suggests ingredients mixed up, so the letters are stirred into a new order

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A dessert that a man called Liam made.
explanation.definitionFit: Semolina is coarse wheat meal, often boiled with milk and sugar as a traditional British milk pudding.

clue.text: Check news story at intervals during weather forecast?

indicators.note: during means in the middle of, so the chosen letters go inside the next piece

parts.note: rain is an example of what a forecast may predict, hence the question mark

indicators.note: at intervals means taking every other letter, skipping the rest

parts.note: the second, fourth, sixth and eighth letters

explanation.surface: A news report on the weather is cut short partway through.
explanation.definitionFit: To check is to hold back or curb, which is what restrain means.

clue.text: Put right about holiday destination in papers, Spain

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other, here the country inside the documents

parts.note: re means concerning
the Med is the Mediterranean, a popular holiday spot
identity papers
E is the international vehicle code for Spain

explanation.surface: A correction is made about a holiday spot mentioned in Spanish newspapers.
explanation.walkthrough: E is Spain's international vehicle code, and the Mediterranean is commonly shortened in British holiday talk.
explanation.definitionFit: To remedy something is to fix or correct it, so remedied matches put right in the past tense.

clue.text: Stepped up to guard chap sleeping

indicators.note: to guard is to surround protectively, so the letters enclose the next piece
in a down clue, up means the word is read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: trod is the past tense of tread
a chap is a man

explanation.surface: A guard steps up to watch over a man who is asleep.
explanation.definitionFit: Dormant means inactive as if asleep, like a volcano or a hibernating animal.

clue.text: Bill admits politician mostly is okay

indicators.note: to admit is to let in, so the letters take another piece inside

parts.note: a bill is an advertisement, AD

indicators.note: mostly means most but not all, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: a member of the Green Party

explanation.surface: A man called Bill lets a politician in, and that is fine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bill' looks like a name or a law; here it is a poster. The politician is a member of the Green Party.
explanation.definitionFit: Agreed! is an exclamation of consent, used just like okay.

clue.text: Two dig ground, attracting small birds

indicators.note: ground means crushed or pounded, so the letters are broken up and reformed

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged
S is the abbreviation for small

explanation.surface: Two people digging the soil attract little birds looking for worms.
explanation.definitionFit: Godwits are long-billed wading birds of the sandpiper family.

clue.text: Confer over wearing one's smartest clothes elsewhere essentially

indicators.note: something wearing clothes is inside them, so the letter goes within the following pieces

parts.note: your Sunday best is your smartest outfit
O is the cricket abbreviation for over

indicators.note: the essence of a word is its core, so only the central letter is kept

parts.note: the middle letter of the nine

explanation.surface: Someone discusses wearing their best clothes somewhere else.
explanation.walkthrough: O goes inside BEST plus W. 'Confer' looks like discuss, but means grant.
explanation.definitionFit: To confer an honour is to grant it, which is what bestow means.

clue.text: Dark colour of river hard to ignore

indicators.note: ignoring something means leaving it out, so that letter is dropped

parts.note: the Humber is an estuary in northern England
H is the pencil abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: A river's murky shade is hard to overlook.
explanation.definitionFit: Umber is a natural brown earth pigment, giving a dark brownish colour.

clue.text: Gym equipment engineer trialled, accepting money originally

indicators.note: accepting means taking in, so the rearranged letters hold another letter
to engineer is to construct, so the letters are built into a new order

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

indicators.note: originally points to the start, so only the first letter is used

parts.note: the first letter of money

explanation.surface: An engineer tests a new piece of gym kit, taking cash for it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Engineer' looks like the person doing the testing; it is the instruction to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: A treadmill is a running machine with a moving belt, standard kit in a gym.

clue.text: Angry plagiarist blows top

indicators.note: losing its top in a down clue means the first letter goes

parts.note: a pirate copies others' work illegally

explanation.surface: A copycat writer loses their temper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Blows top' doubles as losing one's temper, matching the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Irate means very angry, furious.

clue.text: Recognise difference in skill behind revolutionary mattress

indicators.note: behind means placed after, so the first piece follows the second
a revolution turns things round, so the word reads backwards

parts.note: a pallet is a straw mattress
art is skill

explanation.surface: Someone spots what is special about the craft of a radical mattress maker.
explanation.definitionFit: To tell two things apart is to distinguish between them, seeing how they differ.

clue.text: Find each job oddly lacking in this state

indicators.note: with the odd-placed letters missing, only the even-placed ones remain

parts.note: the second, fourth, sixth, eighth and tenth letters

explanation.surface: Finding work is hard in this particular state.
explanation.definitionFit: Idaho is a state in the north-western United States.

clue.text: Fashionably faded vest — one was hedonistically exhibiting it?

indicators.note: exhibiting means putting on display, so the answer is shown inside the words before

parts.note: letters running across four words

explanation.surface: A vest was worn by someone pleasure-seeking, showing off its trendy worn look.
explanation.definitionFit: Stonewashed fabric, usually denim, is washed with abrasives to look faded and worn, a fashion style.
